Restate only the main (public) question.
Compute \(19 \times 32 + 6 \times 15\).

First, calculate \(19 \times 32\):
\[19 \times 32 = 19 \times (30 + 2) = (19 \times 30) + (19 \times 2) = 570 + 38 = 608.\]

Next, calculate \(6 \times 15\):
\[6 \times 15 = 6 \times (10 + 5) = (6 \times 10) + (6 \times 5) = 60 + 30 = 90.\]

Now, add the results together:
\[608 + 90 = 698.\]

To double-check the main result, let's verify using an alternative order of operations:
\[19 \times 32 = 608,\]
\[6 \times 15 = 90,\]
\[608 + 90 = 698.\]

The answer is verified to be 698.
